_about: Korean realizer declarations: orthography, case particles, lexicon, endings, expression candidates per frame, and the reading rules the semantic check applies. Particle mates, the inflection grammar, negation, numerals, senses and romanization are reused from styles/한국어.json through its parser; nothing here repeats them.

pack_keys._about: Names the pack itself uses for these fields.

compound._about: The engine's compound subject (owner words, then item words) is said by juxtaposition.

before._about: A clause said before 전: its predicate in the nominal form (-기), whatever the register.

after._about: A clause said before 뒤: its predicate in the past adnominal form (-(으)ㄴ), whatever the register.

turn._about: The turn of a conversation, by its number (goal W4).

numbers._about: How a number is said. Digits by default; numeral words (native Korean before a counter) when an expression asks for them.

person._about: The persons of a conversation (meaning.json: holders). user: the words the user says of themself, by the case a reply's part gives the holder (a part with no case, or a holder said juxtaposed before what it holds: default); the reading the semantic check parses says the user so, and each word it says is one the pack groups with its first person (임자자리말 나; 자리말 나, 내); the humble forms (저, 제) are the user's words in a polite register, turned like the others when a holder is named with them (제 룸메이트 -> 룸메이트). addressee: the user is not said in a topic or a subject, juxtaposed before what they hold, or as a possessor (zero anaphora), and a predicate that agrees with them takes the honorific stem -(으)시- (a stem that ends in ㄹ drops it: 알 -> 아시; a negated predicate takes it on the negation's auxiliary: 같지 않으십니다). Round 5 (request G4-2): the user is not said either as a member of a list its particle joins (with: 오다와 합쳐서 … 있으십니다; 자두는 오다와 똑같이 4개 있으십니다), where the clause's predicate honours the list. The user left unsaid is always said by the honorific of a predicate in the same clause; a clause without one is not said (the grammar refuses it). The user in any other case is not declared, and a clause that needs it is not said.

repair._about: The pack's own label for a repair: the word its repair note encloses.

answer_yes._about: The pack's own yes: the word its answer that two counts are the same begins with.

answer_no._about: The pack's own no: the word its answer that two counts differ begins with.

ask_hon._about: To ask, said of the one addressed: the stem with the honorific.

quote_go._about: The ending that closes a quotation before a verb of saying.

count._about: The user's count: the user is not said, the existence verb takes the honorific (사과는 3개 있으십니다; an answer: 3개 있으십니다).
A place's count: the things are in the place (창고에는 상자가 5개 있습니다).

count_none._about: A count of zero: not even one (민수 사과는 하나도 없습니다; an answer: 하나도 없습니다).

count_unknown._about: A vague count: the holder has the thing, how many cannot be known (우나는 배가 있지만 몇 개인지 알 수 없습니다).

transfer._about: To the user (request G4-2): said from the receiver's side, the user not said and 받다 honouring them (오다에게서 자두 2개를 받으셨습니다); the pack reads 받다 by its role swap.
Into a place: the giver put the things there (창고에 상자 3개를 뒀습니다).
Out of a place: the receiver took the things from it (창고에서 상자 3개를 가져갔습니다).
From one place to another: the things were moved (상자 3개가 북쪽 창고에서 남쪽 창고로 옮겨졌습니다).

known._about: The user's thing is known, the relation never came up (이 대화에서 가지신 사탕의 위치는 나온 적이 없습니다).

total._about: A total that includes the user (request G4-2): the user is not said, the others are joined with 과/와 before 합쳐서, and the existence verb honours the list (오다와 합쳐서 자두가 8개 있으십니다).

same_count._about: The user holds as many as the others (request G4-2): the thing first, the others with 과/와, 똑같이, and the existence verb honours the list (자두는 오다와 똑같이 4개 있으십니다).
The user does not hold as many as the others (request G4-2): the count of the thing, the others with 과/와, and the negated verb honours the list on its auxiliary (자두 수가 오다와 같지 않으십니다).

heard._about: The user's thing never came up: the user is not said, the thing is said as the one they have, honoured (이 대화에서 가지신 사탕에 대한 말은 나온 적이 없습니다).

recipient_corrected._about: A receiver corrected in place (request G4-1): the same event, who received before and who received now, each said as having received (같은 사건 "…"에서 준호가 받은 것을 도현이 받은 것으로 고쳤습니다); the user is not said and 받다 honours them (…에서 준호가 받은 것을 받으신 것으로 고쳤습니다).
A receiving side that is a place, corrected in place: the side the things went to, from the old to the new (같은 사건 "…"의 받는 쪽을 북쪽 창고에서 남쪽 창고로 고쳤습니다).

chain_statement._about: Why from the trace graph (goal W4): a statement the answer rests on, with its turn.

count_change._about: The user's count changed (가지신 사탕은 3개에서 5개가 되었습니다).

change_withdrawn._about: A change of the user's count withdrawn (가지신 사탕이 3개에서 5개가 된 것은 취소했습니다).
An earlier value of the user's count withdrawn (가지신 사탕의 앞선 값 5개는 취소했습니다).

rules._about: Each rule said in words, by its id. The id itself is never said; it stays in the trace.

coordination._about: Clauses of one frame said in one sentence: every clause before the last says no copula (gapped); a verb there takes the joining ending -고 (사과는 3개 있으시고, 아라는 2개입니다).

subordinate._about: An event an answer is relative to in time: its clause first, its predicate in the form the following noun governs (전 takes -기, 뒤 takes -(으)ㄴ), then the noun with 에 and the topic 는.

ellipsis._about: A given role is not said at all (zero anaphora). An answer keeps only its focus.

readings._about: How the pack parser's reading of a clause maps back onto frame roles. Used only by the semantic check; independent of the expressions above.

count_none._about: Having none of a thing is read as the count zero, not as a denied count.

slot_words._about: The question word that asks for a role, by the role's particle (the pack's slot particles).

follow_ups._about: Questions about the conversation's own last reply, by kind: why_last asks why the last answer or correction came out so (the bare why word); repairs asks what a reading changed. Only these phrasings, compared after punctuation.

learning._about: Expression learning from user sentences. live: false means a user's way of speaking never enters replies unless this file declares live: true. Learned expressions serve only the conversation they came from.
